Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace offer: initial manifest and account questions

Hi Priya — great questions, thanks for sending the draft. Quick answers up front and then I'll detail next steps: 

1) SAS rotation: use short-lived SAS with a KeyVault-backed automation (our recommendation). The manifest can reference a pre-signed blob URL during validation, but the published offer should use the marketplace image URI (publisher-managed) or a continuous publish pipeline that rotates SAS before the validation window.

2) Telemetry/CORS: telemetry endpoints for usage reporting can remain locked down if you ship an agent that pushes telemetry outbound. If the offer uses client-side web callbacks during validation, Azure may hit endpoints — we usually add an allowlist entry for msft-validation.* during the validation window and remove it post-publish.

3) Co-sell metadata: required fields arepartnerOfferType, resaleChannel (if applicable), and the Seller Id linked to your MPN. Also include contact email and partnerProfileUri. I'll paste a template below.

Next steps: 
- Laura can confirm the billing type (transactable vs lead gen) and whether Acme should enable direct purchase.
- Tessa and I will triage the manifest against Azure's validation checklist and produce a short remediation list. 

I'll run a quick validation pass and share an annotated manifest by EOD.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Hi Priya — thanks for the draft. A few billing and activation notes: 

- If Acme wants transactable billing (customers buy directly in Azure Marketplace), you must provide an offer with at least one Plan configured with pricing tiers. That affects VAT/tax handling and refunds flows.
- For co-sell, confirm whether you want Redwood to be listed as a referral/reseller or to join the Microsoft co-sell program as a pure partner referral. The co-sell enablement process requires an MPN ID and Partner Centre relationship setup; both are doable but take different lead times (typically 2-4 business days to confirm relationships once the proper forms are submitted).
- We can pre-authorize a sample invoice schema to speed the first transactable sale.

I recommend toggling transactable off for the initial publish to avoid unexpected billing events while validation completes; we can flip it on once the validation and telemetry checks are green.

Laura Bennett
Director, Billing & Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Folks — tagging the technical validation notes from my quick pass. I ran the draft manifest through an internal checklist and the items that need attention before we request Microsoft validation are below: 

- Image packaging: the draft references a custom VM extension that runs at boot. Azure validation requires the extension to return a 0 exit code within the validation sandbox and not attempt to reach blocked endpoints. We should include a small smoke-test script in the image that exits with 0 and reports a health file to the blob.
- SAS token: remove long-lived SAS from the published artifact. Use temporary pre-signed blob URLs for validation only; move artifacts to an official publisher storage account prepped in Partner Centre before final publish.
- Telemetry: remove any client-side cross-origin redirects. Switch to an agent push model or provide a stub endpoint for validation that returns 200 for the msft-validation user-agent.
- Offer metadata: missing partnerOfferType in the manifest; add partnerProfileUri and the MPN seller id.

I attached a short remediation plan (co-sell-enablement-notes.pdf) and a cleaned checklist. Once Priya confirms she'll update the image packaging and metadata fields, we can submit to Marketplace Validation. Also recommend scheduling a 30-min handoff with Microsoft validation if this is the first offer from Acme.

Thanks — Tessa
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
